items.title: 56800_John Simmons oral history interview
items.q: Now they all stayed on the bandstand... Ben Tharp... playing drums and myself.

ctx.x: And when he said that, I went right up against his melon. I broke his dentures, his nose, his eye glasses. Now the waiters to the rescue. Now the cashier was Max Gordon's brother-in-law, Max Gordon, the owner of the club didn't like him. And he was paralyzed on one side. The waiter has my arms pinned behind me and the cashier is going to throw a punch at me. I say well how do you like that. To myself. So by this waiter holding my arms behind me, I just tightened up and put both feet in his chest. (Laughter). He…

And on the bandstand, was Clyde Hart. He was a pretty good piano player. He always ran around with Art Tatum and smoked a cigar. He was good for chord structure. He played somewhat on the style of Teddy Wilson. He was out here with Stuff Smith's band also. Same time that Cozy Cole was with the band. I think that band, speaking of Stuff's band. He had

Bernard Addison playing guitar. Jonah Jones, Cozy, I can't remember the bass player's name and Clyde Heart. But anyway, at the Vanguard, Clyde was playing the piano, Buster Bailey playing clarinet, Charlie Shavers was playing trumpet. Ben Tharp, Ben, Ed Thigpen's father, playing drums and myself. Now they all stayed on the bandstand. Lester looked up and said whispering grass, (laughter), didn't any of them move off the bandstand. They no fighters, no heart for fighting. Clyde Heart's got his fingers and things…
